results.info:
This simplified carbon footprint aims to estimate the greenhouse gas emissions from your activity, and therefore your contribution to climate disruption as well as your potential dependence on fossil fuels, which are vulnerabilities. 

By ratifying the Paris Agreement, the European Union has committed to achieving carbon neutrality by 2050. To contribute to this goal, your cinema should reduce its impact by 5% per year. 

We therefore invite you to complete this simplified carbon footprint again next year to check that you are on the right track!

difference.button: Explanation of differences between Bilan Carbone® and the {type} export
difference.otherEmissionsAvalTitle: Accounting for other downstream emissions - Visitor and customer travel
difference.otherGasTitle: GHGs not counted in the GHG Protocol
difference.dependance: The regulatory GHG inventory does not include the "Dependency use" sub-category, because the notion of dependency is not addressed in this method.
difference.dependanceGHG: The GHG Protocol does not include the "Dependency use" sub-category, because the notion of dependency is not addressed in this method.
difference.waste: The regulatory GHG inventory includes all emissions from waste recycling in the waste generator's inventory, whereas Bilan Carbone® only assigns the waste generator the burden of waste collection and transport. Thus, emission factors with a value of 41 kgCO₂e/t in the tool are those used for Bilan Carbone®, while values that include material regeneration (the recycling process, for emission factors labeled "Recycling" or "Average end of life") are used for BEGES-R. The emission factor displayed in BC+ is only the one used for Bilan Carbone®, but BEGES-R export calculations do use emission factors related to recycling or average end of life from ADEME. Here are the emission sources related to this topic:
difference.missingCaract1: Uncharacterized emission sources are not counted in {type}, which causes unwarranted differences with Bilan Carbone® if you chose to display unvalidated emission sources.
difference.missingCaract2: You have not provided characterizations for all emission sources in your study. Please edit and add the characterization for the following emission sources:
difference.immobilisation1: The GHG Protocol accounts for all emissions related to constructing an asset in the year it is acquired. Bilan Carbone®, on the other hand, amortizes emissions over several years, which explains part of the differences between these two formats.
difference.otherEmissionsAval: Accounting for visitor or customer travel is optional under the GHG Protocol. If these emissions are calculated nonetheless and are not operated, they will not be counted in this export, because there is no suitable category in which to report them.
difference.otherEmissionsAmont: Some emissions are not accounted for under the GHG Protocol, particularly when the associated activities are not operated by the organization. This is for example the case for upstream electricity production and line losses. In the regulatory GHG inventory, these are counted in category 6.1 dedicated to other indirect emissions, but as there is no equivalent category in the GHG Protocol, these emissions are not included.
difference.otherGas1: Only GHGs that are part of the Kyoto Protocol (CO₂, CH₄, N₂O, HFC, PFC, SF₆) are counted under the GHG Protocol. Emissions related to other GHGs (contrail cirrus, NF3, other refrigeration or process GHGs) are therefore counted in Bilan Carbone®, but not in the GHG Protocol.
difference.marketBased: Some of the differences between market-based GHG Protocol and Bilan Carbone® simply come from the difference in results between <green>location-based</green> and <purple>market-based</purple> methods.
difference.fabrication: You used emission factors based on distances (passenger.km, ...) for operated vehicles. Emissions related to manufacturing these vehicles are not accounted for in the GHG Protocol. Please use the Fixed assets category for manufacturing emissions from vehicles acquired in the inventory year.

difference.unexplainedDifference: Some differences cannot be explained for your study and may be related to calculation issues in the tool. If you can, please contact us at <supportLink>support</support>.

glossary.title: Glossary
glossary.uncertaintyPerPostDescription: Note: the size of the circles on this chart is proportional to the number of emission sources entered within the category, not to the total emissions of the category (which can be seen on the horizontal axis). This makes it possible to see which categories were worked on in the most detail, and to assess whether that is relevant given the importance of the associated emissions, since it is generally more relevant to work in detail on the largest emission categories. The following charts also help visualize this effect.
glossary.uncertaintyPerPostDescription2: Furthermore, the more emission sources there are within a category, the lower that category's uncertainty will be. This is because two uncertainties offset each other, since it is generally not certain that the error is in the same direction. To give a concrete example, when measuring two ropes, you may overestimate the length of the first and underestimate the second. Therefore, the uncertainty on the length of the sum of the two ropes will be less than the sum of the two uncertainties taken separately.

results.simplifiedFeedback:
Congratulations! You have just completed the simplified carbon footprint of your cinema. This is an excellent introduction to carbon accounting!



By ratifying the Paris Agreement, the European Union has committed to achieving carbon neutrality by 2050. To contribute to this goal, your cinema should reduce its impact by 5% per year. The simplified carbon footprint you have just obtained can already help you better understand how to reduce your impact by identifying your most emission-intensive activities.



We invite you to complete this simplified carbon footprint again next year to check that you are on the right track, or, even better, to carry out a full Bilan Carbone® in order to achieve a more accurate estimation of your emissions and develop a proper transition plan! To get started, nothing could be simpler: you can train in the method, contact us at count@cut-collectif.fr, or get in touch with another Bilan Carbone® provider.

glossary.validatorEmailDescription: For each Bilan Carbone®, one or more validators can be assigned. They are responsible for validating emission sources once these have been entered by the contributors and editors of the study. By default, only validated emissions appear in your results, but you can change this behavior via the "Settings" menu.
glossary.studyDates: Reference year of the carbon footprint
glossary.studyDatesDescription: Please provide the reference period for your simplified carbon footprint. Ideally, the reference period should be twelve months.
glossary.realizationDatesDescription: This is the period during which you will work on completing the study: filling in emission sources, generating exports, etc. These dates are not mandatory and you can always access the study outside the period entered.
glossary.typeDescription: The new version of the Bilan Carbone® method introduces three maturity levels for organizations' Bilan Carbone® assessments. For more details, we invite you to visit <link>this page</link>.
glossary.visibilityDescription: Choose whether your study should be shared with your team, meaning accessible to all colleagues listed on the My organization > My team page, or confidential, meaning accessible only to people you add on your study framing page. Your organization administrators have access to all studies, whether shared with your team or confidential.
glossary.exportsDescription: Results are displayed by default in Bilan Carbone® format, but you can also obtain results in the formats required by several other carbon accounting methods, such as the regulatory GHG inventory, which is the French regulatory method.
glossary.controlDescription: Control mode is information requested by certain carbon accounting methods, such as the regulatory GHG inventory or the GHG Protocol. To obtain results in the formats required by these methods, you will need to characterize the various emission sources during data entry, which will determine which existing categories within these methods (the equivalent of categories and sub-categories in the Bilan Carbone® method) the emissions will be allocated to. Control mode applies to all exports you have selected. Depending on the control mode selected, the characterizations available for the various emission sources vary. For more detail on control modes, we invite you to consult the methodological guides for the methods in question. We strongly recommend using the "Operational Control" control mode, which is by far the most common.
glossary.duplicationOptionsDescription: When duplicating a study, you can choose to invite the same team members and contributors from the original study into the new one. This helps maintain continuity of collaboration.

bc.disclaimerExcel1: Please note that the results you obtain here come solely from the Count simplified carbon footprint and must not under any circumstances be used as Bilan Carbone® results.
bc.disclaimerExcel2: The process you followed using the Count tool is NOT a Bilan Carbone® process, even though the results obtained can already help you better understand how to reduce your impact by identifying your most emission-intensive activities.

bc.disclaimerExcel5: A Bilan Carbone® follows a precise methodology and must meet a number of objective criteria. ressources.title: Resources
ressources.description:
The COUNT impact calculator is accredited by ABC. It was built using various emission factor sources (ADEME Base Empreinte, EcoInvent, Boavizta, CNC in particular). Other emission factors were specifically developed for the tool by Resilio.

Calculation assumptions were built from:

- 15 full carbon footprints completed with the CINEO cinema group

- Multiple interviews with cinema stakeholders (suppliers, integrators, independent operators, cinema chains, etc.)

- Visits to cinemas of various types
ressources.france2030: As part of the France 2030 Plan, the “Green Alternatives 2” scheme, endowed with €25M over 3 waves and operated by Banque des Territoires (Caisse des Dépôts group) with the Ministry of Culture, the Ministry for Ecological Transition, and the General Secretariat for Investment, aims to accelerate the ecological transition of cultural businesses. Of the 51 applications received for the first wave, 13 projects were selected, including the project led by CUT!

glossaryDescription.DechetsDirects: This category covers all emissions related to managing waste produced (collection and treatment) within the organization. It is divided into sub-categories, each covering a type of waste.
glossaryDescription.IntrantsBiensEtMatieres: This category covers emissions related to the various flows of goods and materials entering the organization. It is divided into sub-categories, each covering a type of material.
glossaryDescription.Immobilisations: All emissions related to purchasing or long-term leasing of durable goods (subject to depreciation by the organization).
glossaryDescription.FinDeVie: This category covers all emissions related to the future end of life of products sold within the reporting period.
glossaryDescription.DeplacementsDomicileTravail: Home-to-work travel for people present within the organization, including temporary workers, subcontractors, and contractors.
glossaryDescription.DeplacementsProfessionnels: Business travel by people within the organization in the course of their professional activity, whether or not the organization owns the means of transport, and whether or not travel occurs during working hours.
glossaryDescription.IntrantsServices: This category covers services received by the organization and its digital usage. Services are often accounted for either via GHG information provided by the organization's service providers, or via emission factors expressed as monetary ratios.
glossaryDescription.Energies: This category groups energy consumption from so-called "fixed" sources: premises, machinery, etc. In a Bilan Carbone®, emissions associated with energy consumption of goods or premises used by the organization must be included, whether it owns or leases them. Energy consumption of vehicles or other "mobile" sources (fossil fuels, organic fuels, electricity) is normally not included in the Energy category, but in the Freight and Travel categories.
glossaryDescription.CombustiblesFossiles: For heating, industrial processes, electricity or steam production.
glossaryDescription.CombustiblesOrganiques: For heating, industrial processes, electricity or steam production.
glossaryDescription.Electricite: For heating, routine use, industrial processes, and on-site electricity production.
glossaryDescription.Agriculture: Enteric fermentation in ruminants, livestock manure, use of nitrogen fertilizers, ...
glossaryDescription.EmissionsLieesAuxProcedesIndustriels: Cement production, process emissions in the semiconductor industry, ...
glossaryDescription.FretInterne: When the departure and arrival points are both within the organizational boundary.
glossaryDescription.ServicesEnApprocheMonetaire: Various services received, accounted for via emission factors expressed as monetary ratios.
glossaryDescription.MatiereDestineeAuxEmballages: To enable transition plan actions targeting packaging, a sub-category is dedicated to materials used for packaging.
glossaryDescription.BiensEtMatieresEnApprocheMonetaire: A sub-category is also dedicated to materials for which emission factors expressed as monetary ratios are used.
glossaryDescription.UtilisationEnResponsabilite: Products sold by the organization within the reporting period over their full lifetime, for which the organization is directly responsible (for example, for a manufacturer of in-flight meal trays, use under direct responsibility corresponds to the energy used to chill and reheat the meal tray).
glossaryDescription.UtilisationEnDependance: Products sold by the organization within the reporting period over their full lifetime, for which the organization is not directly responsible but whose activity contributes to emissions (for example, for a manufacturer of in-flight meal trays, use under dependency corresponds to emissions from the entire flight).

baseModal.title: Information for GHG-P exports
baseModal.description: Indicate here whether your EF applies under the location-based method, or under the market-based method. This distinction applies only if your EF is used in the Electricity sub-category of the Energy category. Reminder:
baseModal.location: The location-based method uses emission factors representing the average electricity mix over defined geographic and temporal boundaries. In France, emission factors are typically of the form "Average mix - Year concerned - France".
baseModal.market: The market-based method uses emission factors representative of electricity produced by power producers with whom the organization is contractually linked via Guarantees of Origin (GOs) purchases, Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs) in the United States, Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs, VPPAs), etc. Any electricity not covered by the contracts mentioned must then be accounted for using emission factors for residual mixes, i.e., electricity mix emission factors from which all electricity covered by those contracts has been removed.
baseModal.conclusion: Bilan Carbone® and regulatory GHG reporting allow only the location-based method; ISO 14064-1 allows both methods, while the GHG Protocol requires double accounting of electricity consumed, once as location-based and once as market-based.

glossary.title: Glossary
glossary.detailedGESDescription: If you know the share of emissions attributable to the different GHGs for your emission factor, you can enter it using this feature. The Bilan Carbone® method does not use this breakdown, because knowing how emissions are split across GHGs complicates results without providing information useful for building the transition plan. This breakdown is useful, however, if you want the various exports offered by BC+.

multipleDescription.introduction: Some emission factors have components, meaning they consist of different emissions from different activities. For example, emission factors for electricity in France are typically split into three components:
multipleDescription.upstream: Upstream, which accounts for emissions related to building electricity production infrastructure and transporting electricity on the grid.
multipleDescription.combustion: Power plant combustion, which accounts for emissions related to electricity production itself (coal combustion, ...).
multipleDescription.loss: Losses, which account for heat loss during electricity transport on the grid.
multipleDescription.conclusion: This disaggregation is not used within the Bilan Carbone® method, but it allows allocating emissions from the different components to categories for exports (for regulatory GHG reporting, using the same example, and if the emission source is "Operated", "upstream", "power plant combustion", and "losses" emissions are allocated to categories 4.1, 1.2, and 4.1 respectively). We strongly recommend not using this feature unless you are familiar with allocations under regulatory GHG reporting.

table.wasteModalContent: Emission factors dedicated to waste recycling (or average end of life when it includes recycling) use a value of 41 kgCO₂e/t instead of the value assigned by Base Empreinte®. This value corresponds to collection, transport, and metal storage operations in Base Empreinte®, and therefore excludes material regeneration, which accounts for most emissions related to recycling. This approach is chosen so as not to penalize recycling, which is nevertheless accounted for in inputs within Bilan Carbone® (an input from recycled material generally emits less than a new input). For regulatory GHG reporting, the Base Empreinte® value will be used in your export. A modal explaining any differences between Bilan Carbone® and regulatory GHG reporting will be available at the top left of this export. For more detail, see annex 1 of the Bilan Carbone® method or the pages on waste in the General Carbon Plan.

difference.warning: Warning: your market-based kWh are not equal to your location-based kWh.
difference.title: Warning - The number of kWh counted differs between the <green>location-based</green> method and the <purple>market-based</purple> method
difference.description: The GHG Protocol requires double accounting of electricity consumed, first via the location-based (location-based method, LBM) method and second via the market-based (market-based method, MBM) method. To do this, simply account for your kWh of energy consumed twice, once using emission factors dedicated to location-based, and a second time using emission factors dedicated to market-based. You must account for the same number of kWh in both methods.
